column6: note

column1: # Leave the id off a new row: the build assigns one and writes it back.
# Why this file exists. `qué`, `dónde`, `cuánto` and `cómo` were well covered by the
# situations the missions teach -- you cannot order a coffee without them. The
# other four were not: `cuándo` had two plain examples outside the health
# passages, `cuál` had two, `quién` four, and `por qué` exactly one. A learner
# could confirm a hotel and describe a symptom but could not ask when the party
# starts, which of two shirts is cheaper, who the new boss is, or why not.
# So each of those four gets what the missions get: a dialogue that puts it in a
# real situation, and a palette of natural alternatives on either side of it --
# the question and the answer, because a question word nobody answers teaches
# half a move.
# The demonstratives ride along at the end. `este`/`ese`/`aquel` are what the
# answer to «¿cuál?» is actually made of, so the choosing dialogue teaches the
# three-way contrast where it really occurs, and the closing section gives the
# `grammar` category the items it was short of.
# ── ¿Cuándo es la fiesta? (model dialogue) ────────────────────────────────────

column2: Oye, Luis, el sábado hay una fiesta en mi casa.
column3: Hey, Luis, there's a party at my place on Saturday.

column2: Empieza a las nueve de la noche.
column3: It starts at nine in the evening.

column2: Muy tarde. Estas fiestas nunca terminan pronto.
column3: Very late. These parties never finish early.
When do I need to get there?

column2: A las nueve o a las diez. Las dos están bien.
column3: At nine or at ten. Either is fine.

column2: Entonces voy sobre las nueve y media.
column3: Then I'll come at about half past nine.

column6: The bare question, for anything with a date.
For opening times rather than an event.
For something with a start time.
The other half of opening hours.
Asks for a date, not a time.

column3: When are you back from holiday?
column6: About a person rather than an event.

column3: How long have you lived here?
column6: Asks when something started and still holds.

column3: How long are you in Madrid for?
column6: Asks when something ends.

column2: Es el sábado por la tarde.
column6: A day and a part of it, without a clock time.

column2: Empieza a las ocho y media.
column3: It starts at half past eight.
column6: The precise answer.

column2: Abre a las diez de la mañana.
column3: It opens at ten in the morning.
column6: Says which ten, which the clock alone does not.
A recurring day rather than one date.
Counts forward instead of naming a date.
An honest answer that still answers.
Approximate on purpose.
For a routine rather than a one-off.

column1: # ── ¿Cuál te gusta más? (model dialogue — and where este/ese/aquel live) ──────

column2: Mira estas camisas. Son muy bonitas.
column3: Look at these shirts. They're very nice.
Yes. Which one do you like better?
This one, the blue one. And you?
I prefer that one, the green one.
And that one over there, the one in the window?
That one over there is very expensive.
Which one shall I buy then?
All right, I'll take this one.

column6: The shortest form of the question.

column2: ¿Cuál te gusta más, este o ese?
column3: Which do you like better, this one or that one?
column6: Names both options, so the answer cannot be vague.
Asks for a recommendation out of several.
The plural — more than one is being chosen.

column2: ¿Cuál de los dos es más barato?
column3: Which of the two is cheaper?
column6: Narrows the field to two and names the test.
Picks one out of a set that is already known.
The near one, with no noun repeated after it.
The one nearer the other person.
Chooses and gives the reason in one line.
Ends the choosing — a decision, not a preference.
Declines to choose, pleasantly.
A polite no to the whole set.

column1: # ── ¿Quién es el nuevo jefe? (model dialogue) ─────────────────────────────────

column2: Buenos días, Marta. ¿Quién es ese señor?
column3: Good morning, Marta. Who's that man?

column2: Es el nuevo jefe. Se llama Carlos.
column3: He's the new boss. His name is Carlos.

column2: Son las compañeras de Carlos. Trabajan con él.
column3: They're Carlos's colleagues. They work with him.
Who do I have the meeting with today?

column2: ¿Y quién más va a la reunión?
column3: And who else is going to the meeting?

column2: Todos nosotros. Es una reunión grande.
column3: All of us. It's a big meeting.

column6: About someone in sight, pointed at with a demonstrative.
The plural, which the singular does not cover.
`quién` after a preposition, where English moves it to the end.
Asks for a role rather than a name.
Ownership is `de quién`, not a word of its own.
About people who are not there yet.
A relationship rather than a name.
The plural answer.
A role, with the one detail that matters.
Places someone by who they belong to.
The answer when there is no answer.

column2: Es una amiga de mi hermana.
column3: She's a friend of my sister's.
column6: Two steps of relationship, which is how it usually comes out.

column3: Shall we go to the cinema tonight?

column2: Esta noche no puedo. Lo siento.

column3: Because I have a lot of work.

column2: ¿Y por qué tienes mucho trabajo ahora?
column3: And why do you have a lot of work now?

column2: Porque mi jefe está de vacaciones.
column3: Because my boss is on holiday.

column2: ¿Y por qué no vamos el viernes?
column3: And why don't we go on Friday?

column2: El viernes sí puedo. Buena idea.
column3: I can on Friday. Good idea.

column2: Entonces el viernes a las ocho.

column6: On its own. Short, and not rude in Spanish.
Softer than the bare question, and very common.
Asks about what was just said.

column3: Why don't you come with us?
column6: A suggestion wearing a question — not a complaint.
About a situation rather than a person.
Asks for a reason and shows surprise at once.
`porque` is one word; `por qué` is two.
The most useful reason there is.

column3: It's just that I don't have time.
column6: Softens a reason, and never starts with `porque`.
A reason with no verb in it at all.
`por qué` inside a statement rather than a question.

column3: Because I get up early tomorrow.
column6: A reason about later, not about now.

column1: # ── este, ese, aquel — near, there, over there ────────────────────────────────

column2: Este libro es mío y ese es de Marta.
column3: This book is mine and that one is Marta's.
column6: The two-way contrast in one line.

column2: Esta silla es nueva, pero aquella es muy vieja.
column3: This chair is new, but that one over there is very old.
column6: Adds the third distance: further off than `ese`.

column3: I want this one, not that one.
column6: Both standing alone, with no noun after them.

column2: ¿Ves aquella casa blanca? Allí vivo yo.
column3: Can you see that white house over there? That's where I live.
column6: `aquel` for something in sight but far away.
Neuter: points at an idea, not at a thing with a gender.
The near neuter — handing something over.
Plural, and still a determiner before its noun.

column2: Estas llaves son de la casa y esas son de la oficina.
column3: These keys are for the house and those are for the office.
column6: Feminine plural, both sides of the contrast.

column2: Esta semana trabajo mucho, pero la próxima no.
column3: This week I'm working a lot, but not next week.
column6: `este` about time rather than space, which is most of its use.

column2: Aquel hotel de la plaza es muy bueno.
column3: That hotel on the square over there is very good.
column6: `aquel` before its noun, the way a determiner normally sits.
